correctness.rationale: In edge coordinates g_i=u_i-u_0, put b_i=c_i sign(g_i)|g_i|^(p-1). Then g'=Ab with A=-diag(1/m_i)-(1/m_0)11^T. The right derivative of the weighted absolute-value norm is a sum of signed velocities on nonzero edges and absolute velocities on zero edges. Expanding by columns of A gives the upper bound sum_i |b_i|B_i for B_i=(W-2w_i)/m_0-w_i/m_i; the off-diagonal contributions can be no larger than sum_(j!=i) w_j/m_0. A one-edge signal achieves B_i in the normalized derivative, hence the supremum is the maximum of the B_i, not every B_i (the wording at line 62 is imprecise; the Finding and displayed proof are clear). The vector field stays inside the initial value bounds, and monotonicity in the mass inner product gives uniqueness without requiring local Lipschitzness for 1<p<2. The right derivative criterion therefore applies at every time; a strictly positive B_i gives immediate increase, while all B_i<=0 force monotonicity by absolute continuity in time. Normalized weights satisfy w_i/W>0 and w_i/W>=(2+m_0/m_i)^(-1), proving feasibility and uniqueness at equality. The frozen checker was inspected but not executed.
